trajectory_summary: This is a short, procedurally competent verify pass on an orphaned-solar lead — the rep moves briskly through address, tenure, existing-system, credit, and utility confirmation. But the call ends without a locked callback time or a captured bill, and a clear enthusiasm/pain signal (suboptimal panel placement due to the tree) was left unexplored.
outcome_dispute: v1 tag is unknown/unclear from metadata; observed outcome is a callback, not a booked or tentative appointment — no day or time was set, only 'pick it up in a couple hours.'

observed_outcome.quote: Okay. Yeah. No problem. We can pick it up in a couple hours then. You have a wonderful rest of your day.
observed_outcome.reasoning: No day or time was locked for either a specialist appointment or a callback — the customer said 'a couple hours' and the rep accepted that vague window without proposing a specific time, so this is a callback outcome, not booked or tentative.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The rep proposed a pre-filled $200/month figure but the customer disputed it as too high and could not confirm a real number while driving, so no reliable bill figure was actually captured on this call — it was deferred to an emailed kWh usage document instead.

interest_reason_audit.reason_quote: I wanted to add panels and possibly a battery.
interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep never explicitly asked 'what interested you in solar' (the customer already has solar, so this was reframed as an orphaned-flow add-on question instead), but the customer's stated want (more panels + battery) was never reinforced or tied back into the close of the call.

primary_coaching_focus.quote: Well, I I, again, I'm driving, and I'm not anywhere near my I can't see my, calendar. So it would be best to, pick up this conversation once I once I get home in a couple hours.
primary_coaching_focus.why: This call had every qualifier pass cleanly (credit, ownership, utility) but ends with zero locked next step — no callback time, no handshake. That's the single highest-leverage fix: a specific rep-proposed window turns a vague callback into a scheduled, trackable touch.

key_moments.quote: No. That's why the panels are located on less than optimal, location.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer volunteers that his existing system underperforms because of shading — a live pain point on his CURRENT solar investment. This is a strong reason to add panels/battery and directly explains his inbound interest, but the rep never asks a follow-up (how much is it underperforming, has he noticed a bill gap) that would have deepened the qualification.

key_moments.quote: Alright. Let me see if I could get a better look here.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer has an existing system with Astrum and wants to add panels/battery — this is the orphaned_flow scenario. The rep captures ownership status and installer name but never asks if the system is currently working or whether Ken has had any issues beyond shading, both of which the orphaned_flow protocol calls for and which would surface useful context for the closer.

key_moments.quote: Last time I checked, it was 849.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer clears the credit qualifier decisively and the rep acknowledges it cleanly and moves on — correct, no issue here, included as a clean qualifier pass.

key_moments.quote: Great. And then I have down here that you're paying about 200 a month on that electric bill. Is that accurate?
key_moments.stewart_read: Rep surfaces a pre-existing bill figure from records rather than asking fresh, and when the customer disputes it ("That sounds a little high") the rep just agrees ("A little high, I would say") without probing for a corrected number or flipping it into motivation.
